newsitem.title: FINLAND: ENSO CEO SAYS MORE HOPEFUL ON PRICES.
newsitem.headline: ENSO CEO SAYS MORE HOPEFUL ON PRICES.

text.p: Jukka Harmala, CEO of forestry group Enso, said on Tuesday he was more optimistic on paper prices than he had been earlier this year.
"The rise in prices should come," he told a news conference after the company's Q1 results.
"In this I'm more optimistic about the whole year than I've been earlier -- above all a clear, if cautious, upturn in pulp prices supports better estimates for the rest of the year."
But he expressed concern about the chance customers may take advantage of current relatively low prices to lay down stocks, prompting more production cuts to support prices later.
"This is a clear risk which would be concentrated on the summer months," he said.

An Enso spokesman saw more capacity in coated fine paper markets, referring to the start-up of a new Enso machine and another at KNP BT in the Netherlands -- although he said the Dutch firm had said it would also shut some smaller machines.
"The net effect is not clear yet" the spokesman said.
